1

Details

Quick pass: the baseline of every channel, measured on the raw samples, against time since the flash. "Recovered" here means the median baseline is back within ±3 mV of its pre-flash level and stays there to 10 ms. This is the electronics coming back. It does not yet say a pulse has its full amplitude again; that is the full analysis (last slides).

Every number is split by beam-pulse intensity: parasitic (~4×10¹² protons) and dedicated (~8.5×10¹²). Pooling them would quote a time that belongs to neither.

Dataset: /eos/experiment/ntof/data/x17/flash_tail (ntof_processing/flash_pull). Summaries: ntof_scint_recovery/flash_summary.py; this pass: quick.py.

After the flash the detectors are blind, then recover: this dataset covers it all

2

Details

The flash time at each detector is tPKUP + C[detector], with C from ntof_processing/flash_timing (walls, divert-off calibration) and run 224572 (plastics, liquids). That is good to ~10 ns, which no result here resolves.

The pulse-shape (PSA) output and the earlier waveform pull both start too late for this: the PSA gives hits, not baselines, and the waveform pull is ±5 µs around DREAM triggers, which start at ~0.5 ms.

Details

Mean of the signal in 100 ns bins, ZS gaps counted as zero, over all channels of the family and all bunches of the class. This is the average waveform: the flash, its tail and the pile-up current of the beam-induced pulses on top.

Walls: the clamp of the diverted signal sits at a fixed level, so its height does not scale with intensity; the tail after it does.

8

Details

Baseline shift: inside the unsuppressed flash block, the median of the samples in each time bin; after it, the median of each zero-suppressed block's 200 leading samples (each block carries 259 samples before its trigger). Medians over every bunch and channel of the detector. Clipped at ±20 mV for display; the flash itself runs off the top.

On the plastics in the first ~100 µs the median includes pile-up of real pulses, so it is the baseline a discriminator would see, not the amplifier's own. The walls' negative excursion is a real undershoot after the flash (checked on single traces in the first look).

10

Details

Dashed lines: steps found in this data, every detector of a family moving at the same run. 224355: walls 0.25 → 0.55 ms. 224401: walls → 0.83 ms, plastics 12 → 31 µs, the liquids first appear. 224450: plastics 31 → 114 µs, liquids 20 → 8 µs, the walls enter the DAQ configuration. 224450–224487: walls and liquids flat, the plastics still moving run to run (114 → 43 → 20 → 126 µs, dedicated). 224401 also moved every plastic ZS threshold by 5 mV; 224355 changed no DAQ setting (so hardware: HV, gain, gate). From 224488 nothing moves, including across 22 July (wall gate delay 200 → 1000 ns) and 23 July (DREAM clock divider), so those are not marked.

Dates of the runs n_TOF never processed are taken from the nearest processed run.

11

Details

The 10–11 July divert-off runs 224356–360 sit in a commissioning epoch, so they are compared with that epoch's divert-on runs (224355, 224361–224400) instead, dedicated: WALA: 551 µs off / 551 µs on, WALB: 551 µs off / 610 µs on, WALC: 551 µs off / 610 µs on, WALD: 551 µs off / 610 µs on.

The divert (blanking) gate switches the wall SiPM signal off for ~1 µs around the flash. In seven runs it was off (N1081B module 6 down on 10–11 July; again 16 July), so the walls recorded the undiverted flash (ntof_processing/FLASH_DIVERT_OFF_RUNS.md). Comparing them says how much of the wall recovery is the gate and how much the SiPMs and their amplifiers.

12

Details

Pulses from pulses.py: baseline from each ZS block's pre-samples, or a running median (200–400 ns chunks) inside the unsuppressed flash block; peaks above 4 mV after smoothing. Width = samples above half height. The liquids (~4 ns wide) are not shown: their width is at the 3 ns bin resolution of the histograms.

The narrow early wall pulses could be the chunked baseline cutting their tails on the steep flash decay, as much as a real shape change; a template fit with a local exponential baseline will tell.

Plastic and liquid pulses are ×2.0 and ×1.5 smaller 2 µs after the flash; wall pulses are not

The amplitude scale of the pulses found against time (dedicated 1.5–3 µs in the title). Gain, or a different particle mix: not yet separated

parasitic

dedicated

±10 %

13

Details

Scale = the 90 % quantile of the amplitudes above a floor (walls and liquids 30 mV, plastics 50 mV), clear of the threshold and of the small-pulse population, interpolated in log amplitude; divided by its own median over 1–10 ms. Production runs, live channels, mean of the four detectors.

Why this is not yet a gain measurement. The spectrum's shape follows the particle mix: fast-neutron recoils (quenched) in the first µs, capture γs from ~0.1 ms, cosmic muons at 30 ms. The dotted lines show the same scale at 30–32 ms differing from 1–10 ms by −15 % (walls) to +35 % (plastics) with no flash nearby -- that is population, not gain. So the early dip is an upper bound on the gain sag. The fixed reference that separates them is next: plastic pulses in coincidence with the wall of the same arm (charged particles crossing the stack, a fixed energy loss per cm), and for the walls the ratio of the two ends of a bar at fixed position.

14

Details

A zero-suppressed block opens only when the signal crosses a fixed threshold relative to the ORIGINAL baseline. While the baseline is 10–19 mV low (10 µs – 1 ms), a pulse must be that much larger to be recorded at all: the effective threshold rises and the small pulses vanish. Above ~30 mV the spectra agree. Ratio in the title: 4–15 mV pulses per pulse above 30 mV at 1–10 ms over the same at 10–100 µs, dedicated.

If the hardware trigger (the sum of a bar's two ends, 26–38 mV) sees the same undershoot, the wall trigger threshold rises by the same amount until ~1 ms.

Fitted on a local baseline, 80 % of the shape is back by ~6.0 µs (plastics), ~7.5 µs (walls), ~60 µs (liquids)

Template fit of isolated pulses: median residual rms over amplitude, dedicated. The walls' last 20 % takes until ~106 µs

parasitic

dedicated

80 % of the early excess gone

15

Details

Recovered shape: the median misfit has lost 80 % of its early excess over the 1–10 ms value (robust to the small bump the plastics show at 0.1–1 ms, which follows the capture-γ population). The tooltips also give the stricter "within +25 % of the 1–10 ms value".

Templates: the median normalised shape of clean pulses 1–10 ms after the flash (one pulse in its ZS block, 30–300 mV), per family (templates.py, templates.npz). Every found pulse is refitted with A·template + b₀ + b₁·t over [−150, +350] ns (walls), [−40, +120] (plastics), [−30, +100] (liquids), so the steep flash tail enters as a local slope instead of biasing the amplitude. Isolated = no other pulse in the window. The misfit floor of the plastics and liquids (~0.1) is the template aligned to the peak sample: a 4–13 ns pulse is not resolved in 1 ns steps. This is the answer to "how far back into the tail can a pulse be reconstructed": from the time its shape is the late-time shape.

16

Details

The plastic minus wall time difference peaks at −15…−5 ns in every arm. Signal window −25…+5 ns; accidentals from +60…+210 ns, scaled by the width ratio. Requiring the wall selects particles that crossed the wall first, which takes out most of the neutron recoils and capture γs that hit the plastic alone. The population is still not fixed (no MIP peak in the beam window: the median is far below the cosmic muons at 30–32 ms, dotted), so this is a cleaner, not a clean, reference.

Signal purity (net / all in the window), dedicated, 1–10 ms: 90%.

The two ends of a wall bar recover together: their ratio moves ≤ 4 % after 2 µs (median of 16 bars)

Median ln(A₁/A₂) of coincident end pairs at fixed position (|Δt| ≤ 10 ns), against its 1–10 ms value; thin: each of the 16 bars

Why this is a gain reference

The two ends of a bar see the same particle. At a fixed position (fixed time difference between the ends) their amplitude ratio depends only on the two gains — not on what particle hit or how much light it made.

A gain loss on one end moves this ratio. A loss common to both ends does not: that half is the next slide.

parasitic

dedicated

±5 %

17

Details

End pairs: the nearest end-2 pulse within ±30 ns of each end-1 pulse (both above 10 mV); accidentals from the same search with end 2 shifted by +500 ns, subtracted bin by bin. Ratio median per 2 ns bin of Δt, minus its own 1–10 ms value, averaged over the bins with |Δt| ≤ 10 ns.

Along the bar the recovery is the same within 7 %; all positions dip together to 0.96

Geometric mean of the two end amplitudes (position-independent light), 90 % quantile above 30 mV, in three position bands; after 3 µs, dedicated, in the title

v < −300 mm

|v| < 150 mm (centre)

v > +300 mm

18

Details

Position v along the bar from the time difference between its two ends, converted per arm and bar with the MM-track calibration of ntof_scint_stack (Δt = a + b·v, b ≈ −0.0136 ns/mm, i.e. ~74 mm/ns; offsets a of −7…+6 ns, so raw Δt bins would mix positions between bars). √(A₁A₂) cancels the attenuation to first order, so the three bands should agree when nothing depends on position. The scale still follows the particle mix, as on the plastic slide; what this slide tests is whether the recovery differs ALONG the bar.

a common-mode gain reference

The plastics' upper edge behind a wall hit (what sets it: light or electronics?), and pulse-height spectra of single-photoelectron / dark pulses if any clear the ZS threshold.

→

per channel

The same curves for each of the 44 channels: which ones are slow, and whether it follows the arm, the bar or the PMT.

→

across the stack

MM tracks (DREAM triggers, from ~0.5 ms) matched to the flash_tail bunches: position perpendicular to the bars, and a fixed-path-length reference.

→

the trigger path

Whether the analog sums feeding the discriminators see the wall undershoot: the trigger rate against time since the flash, from the DREAM data.

The baseline is a necessary condition. A PMT or SiPM can be back on baseline with its gain still low; only the pulses can tell.

Intensity stays a split, never a pool. So do the wall divert state and the 22 July gate change.

19

Details

Inputs: the flash_tail products (raw blocks, 0–10 ms and 30–32 ms), the official PSA hits for comparison, and the stage-3 MM tracks / scint_stack tables for the position step. The MM tracks exist only on DREAM triggers, so position dependence can be studied from ~0.5 ms on, not in the first µs.

What this does not rule out

A common gain sag is not separated from the particle mix.

A loss on one end of a wall bar is ruled out (the end ratio moves ≤ 4 % after 2 µs). A loss common to both ends, and the plastics' slow last ~15 % to ~0.5 ms, can still be gain or a changing particle mix: upper bounds, not measurements.

A sample of the campaign.

~40 bunches per run (2 raw files), 6 files for the divert-off runs and 224572. Ample for medians; thin for rare configurations.

Pile-up on the plastics.

In the first ~100 µs the plastics are a continuous pulse train; their "baseline" there is what a discriminator sees, not the amplifier's.

The trigger path is not measured.

The undershoot is on the digitized signal. Whether the analog sum feeding the wall/plastic discriminators sees it depends on where it is split off.

Time base to ~10 ns.

Per-detector flash offsets, not per channel: irrelevant at these times, not good enough for anything inside the first 100 ns.
